observation.visible_scene: A split-level (half-above, half-underwater) view of clear turquoise water. A curved waterline divides the frame: above it a thin band of rippling, sun-glaring surface; below it the shallow seabed, lit by a dense web of bright white caustic light patterns that spread across the textured bottom.
visible_changes: The caustic light webs on the underwater bottom continuously morph, stretch, merge and shimmer from frame to frame as the surface waves refract the sunlight.
The ripples and bright reflections on the water surface above the waterline change shape and position throughout the clip.

The curved waterline drifts slightly downward within the frame over the excerpt, so the above-water surface band grows a little taller, consistent with a small upward camera tilt rather than a physical rise of the scene.
A dark, thin linear object (rope-like or an edge) appears and becomes more visible at the top-right corner in the later frames.
outside_clip_unknowns: The cause of the surface waves and the camera's platform (handheld, mounted, or on a vessel) are not shown.
The identity of the dark linear object at the top-right and the scene beyond the frame edges are not visible.
Whether the excerpt begins or ends mid-process cannot be judged; both boundaries are arbitrary crops.
uncertain_details: Whether the slight downward shift of the waterline is camera tilt or a change in water level relative to the lens.
The exact material of the seabed (sand vs rock) and the precise nature of the dark line.
